problem:
A particle $P$ is moving in the $x$-$y$ plane. Its position vector relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by

$$
r=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle at time $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t))⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we substitute in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ),4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )⟩ \\  & =⟨-4(0),4(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ we calculate the magnitude of $v(\frac{\pi }{2}),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|v(\frac{\pi }{2})| & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
